variables.label: Final survey weight
variables.definition: Final combined landline/cell-phone weight used to produce population estimates from respondents.
variables.universe: completed 2024 BRFSS adult interviews
variables.suppression_rules: Estimates are subject to BRFSS reliability/precision guidance; consult the annual quality report and table footnotes.
variables.comparability_notes: Use with the complex survey design. Delaware report estimates are weighted, not raw respondent percentages.

variables.label: Fair or poor general health
variables.definition: GENHLTH asks respondents to rate general health; `_RFHLTH` groups fair/poor versus good or better.
variables.universe: adults age 18+
variables.geography: Delaware; counties only where report/sample supports them
variables.suppression_rules: Follow annual codebook and Delaware report reliability notes.
variables.comparability_notes: Concept aligns with CHR poor/fair health and AHR high health status, but CHR/AHR may model or invert the indicator.

variables.label: Physically or mentally unhealthy days
variables.definition: Raw items count days in the past 30 when physical or mental health was not good; calculated fields group the number of days.
variables.unit: days in past 30 or weighted percent
variables.universe: adults age 18+
variables.comparability_notes: CHR poor physical/mental health days are modeled county estimates and should not be treated as raw Delaware BRFSS county observations.

variables.label: No health-care coverage, ages 18-64
variables.definition: Derived coverage indicator for adults younger than 65 from reported primary source of health coverage.
variables.universe: adults age 18-64
variables.comparability_notes: Age universe differs from Census civilian noninstitutionalized population, CHR under-65/adult measures, and AHR total-population uninsured measures.

variables.label: No leisure-time physical activity
variables.definition: No physical activity or exercise other than the regular job during the past 30 days.
variables.universe: adults age 18+
variables.comparability_notes: Matches the basic concept used by CHR/AHR physical inactivity, but downstream products may age-adjust/model and use different pooled years.

variables.label: Current cigarette smoking and current e-cigarette use
variables.definition: Current cigarette smoking derives from lifetime smoking and current frequency; current e-cigarette use derives from ever/current use items.
variables.universe: adults age 18+
missing_codes: 9=do not know/refused/missing in calculated risk-factor fields
variables.comparability_notes: Cigarette definition aligns closely with CHR and AHR adult smoking. E-cigarette is separate and must not be added to cigarette smoking without handling overlap.

variables.label: Body mass index and weight-status category
variables.definition: BMI calculated from self-reported height and weight, stored with two implied decimal places; category groups underweight, normal, overweight, and obese.
variables.universe: adults with usable height and weight
missing_codes: blank or codebook-defined missing when height/weight unusable
variables.comparability_notes: Self-report bias and age adjustment/modeling distinguish it from clinical BMI and CHR/AHR modeled obesity.

variables.label: Binge drinking
variables.definition: Derived indicator based on consuming 5+ drinks for men or 4+ for women on an occasion during the past 30 days.
variables.universe: adults age 18+
variables.comparability_notes: AHR excessive drinking combines binge and heavy drinking, so it is broader than this field alone.

variables.label: Diagnosed diabetes and prediabetes
variables.definition: Self-report of clinician-diagnosed diabetes (with pregnancy-only/borderline distinctions) and prediabetes/borderline diabetes.
variables.universe: adults age 18+; prediabetes item universe follows questionnaire skips
variables.comparability_notes: Self-reported diagnosis excludes undiagnosed disease; do not merge diabetes and prediabetes or compare directly with claims/clinical prevalence.

variables.label: Preventive services and screening
variables.definition: Questionnaire items record influenza/pneumococcal vaccination, HIV testing, and age/sex-specific cancer screening histories; report indicators apply stated look-back windows and eligibility ages.
variables.universe: measure-specific adult age/sex/organ eligibility groups
variables.suppression_rules: Follow codebook and report table reliability rules.
variables.comparability_notes: Exact age band, organ status, and screening interval are essential; apparent matches across CHR/AHR may use different guideline vintages.

crosswalk_hints.notes: Strong conceptual match to CHR Adult Smoking and AHR Smoking; align year, age adjustment, modeling, and geography.
Only compare after enforcing age 18-64 and reconciling survey question/source with ACS/SAHIE.
Same no-leisure-activity concept feeds multiple health rankings, but county products may model several years.
AHR may publish the positive inverse (high health status); do not compare signs without normalization.

sources.research_notes: The Delaware report is a public table-level codebook and CDC supplies a complete public-use variable codebook. The catalog's measure phrases are not column names; use CDC raw/calculated names. Question wording, availability, and derived-variable versions change by year.

codebook_artifacts.notes: Documents submission fields/workflow; not a substitute for the report's analytic definitions.

codebook_artifacts.authority: Delaware Cancer Registry and Delaware Division of Public Health
codebook_artifacts.applies_to: Prior five-year edition
codebook_artifacts.notes: Useful for version comparison; methodology/site definitions may differ from 2018-2022 edition.

variables.label: Cancer incidence count
variables.definition: Number of reportable newly diagnosed malignant cancers among Delaware residents; in-situ bladder cancers are included under the report's exception.
variables.universe: Delaware resident reportable cancer diagnoses, 2018-2022, submitted by the report cutoff
variables.suppression_rules: Frequencies below 16 are not presented under the report confidentiality standard.
variables.comparability_notes: Case counts depend on reportability, submission cutoff, multiple-primary rules, and site/histology coding; not survey prevalence.

variables.label: Age-adjusted cancer incidence rate
variables.definition: New cancer cases per 100,000 population, directly age-adjusted to the 2000 U.S. standard population using 19 age groups.
variables.universe: Delaware resident reportable cases and corresponding population
variables.suppression_rules: Rates based on small case counts are not calculated/presented per the report's 16-case confidentiality/reliability rule.
variables.comparability_notes: Compare only age-adjusted rates using the same standard, site definition, period, and registry completeness.

variables.label: Age-specific cancer incidence rate
variables.definition: New cancer cases per 100,000 persons within a specified age group.
variables.universe: specified age group
variables.comparability_notes: Age-specific rates are not age-adjusted and should not be compared to the report's age-adjusted rate column.

variables.label: Cancer mortality count
variables.definition: Deaths of Delaware residents with cancer as the underlying cause, classified using death certificates and ICD-10.
variables.universe: Delaware resident deaths in stated period
variables.comparability_notes: Mortality is death-certificate underlying cause and is distinct from registry incidence and cancer prevalence.

variables.label: Age-adjusted cancer mortality rate
variables.definition: Cancer deaths per 100,000 population, age-adjusted to the 2000 U.S. standard population.
variables.universe: Delaware resident deaths and population
variables.comparability_notes: Do not compare with incidence rate or crude mortality; align ICD-10 cause grouping and age standard.

variables.label: Rate confidence interval
variables.definition: Lower and upper 95% confidence limits surrounding a published incidence or mortality rate.
variables.universe: same as parent rate
variables.suppression_rules: Not released when parent rate is unavailable.
variables.comparability_notes: Use intervals when judging apparent subgroup/county differences; overlapping intervals are not a complete significance test.

variables.label: Cancer trend annual percent change
variables.definition: Joinpoint-derived annual percent change in an age-adjusted incidence or mortality series; 2020 is excluded from modeled 2008-2022 trends as a pandemic anomaly.
variables.universe: annual Delaware rate series for selected cancer site/outcome
variables.comparability_notes: APC is a modeled slope, not simple endpoint percent change; honor joinpoint segments and the 2020 exclusion.

variables.label: Primary cancer site grouping
variables.definition: SEER-style site group defined from ICD-O-3 topography and histology; examples include lung C340-C349, female breast C500-C509, prostate C619, and colon/rectum C180-C189/C199/C209/C260 with listed exclusions.
variables.universe: reportable registry cases
variables.time_granularity: coding version applies to 2001+ diagnoses as stated
missing_codes: unknown primary site per registry coding
variables.comparability_notes: Never crosswalk by label alone; preserve ICD-O-3 inclusion/exclusion rules and edition.

variables.label: Cancer disparity strata
variables.definition: Published rates/counts stratified by sex, race/ethnicity, and county under report category definitions.
variables.universe: cases/deaths with usable demographic/geographic values
variables.comparability_notes: Hispanic ethnicity and race are not mutually exclusive until combined categories are constructed; definitions differ from single-race Census tables.

crosswalk_hints.notes: Match site-code set, 2000 U.S. standard, registry period, and inclusion of in-situ bladder.
Potential match to AHR/CDC mortality measures only with aligned ICD-10 grouping and period.
Compare rates, not raw counts, and retain uncertainty/suppression.

sources.research_notes: This is an aggregate report rather than a downloadable case-level dataset, but its official methodology and Appendix B constitute a strong public analytic codebook. Cases were reported through November 2024 for the 2018-2022 report; late reporting can revise counts.

variables.source_variable_name: Measure_B.measureId; name; description; format; population; unitType; precision; source; subpopulations; isWeightPositive
variables.label: API measure metadata
variables.definition: GraphQL measure object identifying a measure and its public description, display format, population, unit, precision, source, subpopulations, and whether a higher value contributes positively to a composite.
variables.universe: published AHR measures
variables.comparability_notes: Use stable measureId rather than label for longitudinal retrieval; metadata/version still must be retained.

variables.source_variable_name: MeasureDatum_B.value; state; dateLabel; startDate; endDate; lowerCI; upperCI; rank; dataNotes
variables.label: API measure observation
variables.definition: GraphQL observation with value, geography, labeled/reference dates, optional confidence interval, rank, and notes.
variables.universe: one measure/geography/subpopulation/time observation
variables.suppression_rules: Publisher/source-specific suppression is conveyed by absent values or data notes.
variables.comparability_notes: Not all observations include CIs. Compare values only when measureId, population/subpopulation, and date interval align.

variables.label: Adult smoking
variables.definition: Percentage of adults who smoked at least 100 cigarettes in their lifetime and currently smoke daily or some days.
variables.universe: adults age 18+
variables.time_granularity: source year/pooled period in measure table
variables.suppression_rules: Source and AHR data notes apply.
variables.comparability_notes: Definition aligns with BRFSS/CHR; AHR presentation may age-adjust and aggregate years/subpopulations.

variables.label: Adult e-cigarette use
variables.definition: Percentage of adults who ever used an electronic cigarette or other electronic vaping product and now use one daily or some days.
variables.universe: adults age 18+
variables.comparability_notes: Separate from cigarette smoking and pregnancy smoking; overlapping users prevent simple addition.

variables.label: Exercise guidelines and no leisure-time activity
variables.definition: Exercise is the percentage meeting federal aerobic and muscle-strengthening guidelines; physical inactivity is no activity beyond the regular job during the past 30 days.
variables.universe: adults age 18+
variables.comparability_notes: These are different endpoints. Physical Inactivity aligns with BRFSS `_TOTINDA`; Exercise requires 150 moderate or 75 vigorous minutes plus 2 strength days.

variables.label: Excessive drinking
variables.definition: Percentage of adults reporting binge drinking (4+ drinks women/5+ men on an occasion in past 30 days) or heavy drinking (8+ drinks women/15+ men per week).
variables.universe: adults age 18+
variables.comparability_notes: Broader than BRFSS `_RFBING6` alone because it is a union of binge and heavy drinking.

variables.label: Population without health insurance
variables.definition: Percentage of the population without private or public health insurance coverage under the measure's stated population definition.
variables.universe: measure-table population (verify age-specific variants)
variables.comparability_notes: Do not assume the same universe as BRFSS ages 18-64, CHR under 65, or ACS civilian noninstitutionalized population.

variables.source_variable_name: Infant Mortality; Maternal Mortality; Low Birth Weight
variables.label: Maternal and infant outcomes
variables.definition: Infant deaths per 1,000 live births, maternal deaths per 100,000 live births under source ICD definitions, and percentage of live births below 2,500 grams.
variables.universe: live births and linked/registered deaths under each source definition
variables.comparability_notes: Align linkage method, death definition, race classification, gestational/birth-weight unknown handling, and pooled years with Delaware Vital/HRSA/March of Dimes.

variables.source_variable_name: Breast Cancer Screening; Colorectal Cancer Screening; Cervical Cancer Screening
variables.label: Cancer screening
variables.definition: Guideline-based percentages for eligible age/sex populations receiving mammography, colorectal tests, or cervical screening within measure-specific intervals.
variables.universe: screening-specific age/sex/organ eligibility
variables.comparability_notes: Eligibility ages and guideline intervals change over time; compare to BRFSS only after reproducing identical eligibility and look-back logic.

variables.label: Adult vaccination
variables.definition: Percentages reporting influenza vaccination in the past 12 months or ever receiving pneumococcal vaccination among adults age 65+.
variables.universe: measure-specific adults/all adults or age 65+
variables.comparability_notes: Keep all-adult flu and age-65+ flu/pneumonia universes separate when crosswalking BRFSS/CHR.

variables.label: Household food insecurity
variables.definition: Percentage of households unable at some time during the year to provide adequate food for one or more household members because of insufficient resources.
variables.universe: households
variables.comparability_notes: Household survey prevalence is not the same as Feeding America's modeled person-level county rate or CHR Food Environment Index.

variables.source_variable_name: Housing Cost Burden; Severe Housing Problems
variables.label: Housing affordability and severe problems
variables.definition: Housing cost burden identifies households spending at least 30% of income on housing; severe housing problems combines overcrowding, high costs, incomplete kitchen, or incomplete plumbing.
variables.universe: occupied households under measure-specific rules
variables.comparability_notes: Do not conflate the 30% burden measure with CHR severe cost burden (>50%), the four-part severe-problems composite, or NLIHC's affordability calculation.

variables.label: Annual average PM2.5
variables.definition: Population exposure to annual average fine particulate matter concentration under the measure's stated source/model.
variables.universe: resident population/area under environmental model
variables.comparability_notes: Can align with CHR v125 only if source model, year, spatial aggregation, and population weighting match.

variables.source_variable_name: Primary Care Providers; Dentists; Mental Health Providers
variables.label: Health-care provider supply
variables.definition: Provider supply rates per 100,000 population using profession-specific source definitions.
variables.universe: providers meeting measure source taxonomy and resident population
variables.comparability_notes: AHR and CHR may use similar source systems but can differ in provider taxonomy, practice status, and year; never combine provider types.

variables.source_variable_name: Income Inequality; Unemployment; Per Capita Income; Poverty
variables.label: Economic conditions
variables.definition: Measure-specific income ratio, unemployment share, per-capita income, and poverty prevalence from federal/statistical sources.
variables.universe: measure-specific households/persons/civilian labor force
variables.comparability_notes: Match denominator and source: AHR unemployment may not equal DOL LAUS or ACS DP03; income inequality may be a percentile ratio, not Gini.

crosswalk_hints.notes: Strong definitional match with BRFSS/CHR; reconcile period and adjustment.
Household survey prevalence; not directly comparable to Feeding America person-level modeled estimates.
Match linked/period method and pooled years with Delaware Vital/HRSA/March of Dimes.
Crosswalk to ACS/CHR/NLIHC only after selecting burden threshold versus composite.
Compare individual provider classes, never the combined label.

sources.research_notes: AHR has a published measure dictionary and a typed GraphQL schema. The catalog lists a very broad set spanning multiple AHR report series; always preserve report edition, measureId, population/subpopulation, date interval, unit, and source. API use requires registration/key and is limited by publisher terms.

variables.source_variable_name: statecode; countycode; fipscode; state; county; year; county_clustered
variables.label: Geographic and release identifiers
variables.definition: State/county codes and names, combined FIPS, release year, and indicator that a small county is represented by a multi-county cluster.
variables.universe: one row per state/county or clustered analytic geography
variables.comparability_notes: A clustered estimate is not a standalone county observation; preserve FIPS as zero-padded text.

variables.source_variable_name: v001_rawvalue; v001_numerator; v001_denominator; v001_cilow; v001_cihigh; v001_flag
variables.label: Premature death
variables.definition: Years of potential life lost before age 75 per 100,000 population, age-adjusted.
variables.universe: deaths before age 75 and population under age 75 in the source period
variables.suppression_rules: Missing when fewer than 20 deaths; flag conveys unreliable or suppressed status.
variables.comparability_notes: Equivalent concept may appear in AHR, but period, age adjustment, and source vintage must match.

variables.label: Poor/fair health and physically/mentally unhealthy days
variables.definition: Modeled adult prevalence of self-rated fair/poor health and average physically or mentally unhealthy days in the past 30 days.
variables.unit: proportion for v002; mean days for v036/v042
variables.universe: adults
variables.suppression_rules: Model/reliability rules documented in technical materials.
variables.comparability_notes: Underlying concepts derive from BRFSS, but CHR county values are modeled and should not be mistaken for direct county survey estimates.

variables.label: Low birth weight
variables.definition: Proportion of live births with birth weight below 2,500 grams.
variables.universe: live births with known birth weight in stated period
categories: flagged unreliable if numerator <20 or relative standard error >20%
variables.suppression_rules: Dictionary flags rates with numerator below 20 or relative standard error above 20% as unreliable.
variables.comparability_notes: Concept matches Delaware vital statistics, HRSA, AHR, and March of Dimes; years, birth-file vintage, and unknown handling can differ.

variables.label: Adult smoking
variables.definition: Proportion of adults who report smoking at least 100 cigarettes in their lifetime and currently smoking every day or some days.
variables.universe: adults age 18+
variables.comparability_notes: Question definition closely matches BRFSS `_RFSMOK3` and AHR Smoking, but CHR uses PLACES/modeling and age adjustment.

variables.label: Uninsured
variables.definition: Proportion of population under age 65 without health insurance coverage.
variables.universe: population under age 65
variables.suppression_rules: SAHIE/source reliability and CHR rules apply.
variables.comparability_notes: Universe differs from BRFSS 18-64 and ACS civilian noninstitutionalized total-population measures; CHR also has separate adult/child uninsured measures.

variables.label: Primary care, mental-health, and dental providers
variables.definition: Provider counts per 100,000 population; primary-care field also provides a population-to-provider ratio.
variables.universe: active providers meeting each source definition and resident population
variables.comparability_notes: Provider taxonomy differs by measure and publisher; do not merge PCP, other primary-care, dentist, and mental-health provider rates.

variables.label: Food environment index and access to exercise opportunities
variables.definition: Food environment is an index combining limited access to healthy foods and food insecurity; exercise access is the proportion with adequate access to locations for physical activity.
variables.universe: resident population/households as defined by component sources
variables.comparability_notes: Food Environment Index is not a food-insecurity rate. Compare its food-insecurity component, not the composite, with Feeding America/AHR.

variables.label: Severe housing problems and components
variables.definition: Proportion of households with at least one of overcrowding, high housing costs, lack of kitchen facilities, or lack of plumbing facilities; auxiliary fields expose selected components.
variables.universe: occupied households
variables.comparability_notes: Composite differs from AHR housing cost burden and Census GRAPI. CHR severe cost burden commonly uses >50%, whereas ACS rental cost bins include 30% and 35% thresholds.

variables.label: Economic and education conditions
variables.definition: Unemployment, income inequality, children in poverty, some college, and high-school completion measures with distinct denominators and sources.
variables.universe: measure-specific labor force, households, children, or student cohorts
variables.suppression_rules: See individual dictionary rows and source notes.
variables.comparability_notes: CHR unemployment is not interchangeable with ACS unemployment or DOL LAUS without aligning residence universe, reference period, and modeling; income inequality is 80th/20th percentile ratio, not Gini.

variables.label: Environmental, transportation, and broadband conditions
variables.definition: Average PM2.5, drinking-water violations, drive-alone share, long commute among solo drivers, and broadband-access share.
variables.universe: measure-specific residents, workers, community-water systems, or households
variables.comparability_notes: Do not compare denominators across commute variables; water violation is an exposure indicator, not water-quality concentration.

crosswalk_hints.notes: Match only to age-adjusted YPLL before 75, not general premature age-adjusted mortality.
Align numerator <2,500g, known-weight denominator, pooled period, and suppression with Vital/HRSA/AHR/March of Dimes.
Definition matches BRFSS/AHR but estimate production differs.
Four-part composite; do not substitute rent burden alone.
Verify underlying source/year before comparison with DOL LAUS or ACS DP03.

variables.label: Resident population estimate
variables.definition: Estimated resident population by sex, race, age, county, and selected cities, with historical counts and percent change.
variables.universe: Delaware residents in stated estimate year
variables.suppression_rules: See table footnotes; no unified rule found.
variables.comparability_notes: Population estimates may be revised and are denominators for rates; do not mix vintages across reports.

variables.label: Marriage count and rate
variables.definition: Number of marriages and marriage rate, with distributions by age, prior marital status, county of occurrence, and time.
variables.unit: events; rate per population specified in table
variables.universe: marriages registered in Delaware under report residence/occurrence definition
variables.comparability_notes: Occurrence-based counts can differ from resident-based rates; keep numerator geography explicit.

variables.label: Live births and birth/fertility rates
variables.definition: Resident live-birth counts and rates, including maternal age, race/ethnicity, education, county, and related denominators.
variables.universe: resident live births in report year
missing_codes: unknown/not stated as table category where published
variables.suppression_rules: Report/table small-number and reliability footnotes apply.
variables.comparability_notes: Crude birth rate and general fertility rate use different denominators; do not label either simply 'birth rate' in cross-source joins.

variables.source_variable_name: Birth outcome tables: birth weight and gestational age
variables.label: Low birth weight and preterm birth
variables.definition: Live births below 2,500 grams and births before 37 completed weeks, reported as counts/rates under report definitions.
variables.unit: births; percent of births with known measure
variables.universe: resident live births with known birth weight or gestational age
variables.geography: state/county and demographic groups where shown
missing_codes: unknown/not stated excluded or displayed per table
variables.comparability_notes: Align known-value denominator, gestational-age measure, period pooling, and small-number treatment with CHR/HRSA/AHR/March of Dimes.

variables.label: Prenatal care initiation/adequacy and Cesarean delivery
variables.definition: Timing and adequacy of prenatal care and vaginal/Cesarean delivery measures derived from birth certificates.
variables.universe: resident live births with required certificate fields
variables.comparability_notes: Do not equate all Cesareans with March of Dimes low-risk NTSV Cesarean; adequacy index and unknown handling must match.

variables.label: Pregnancies and pregnancy rate by outcome
variables.definition: Total pregnancies composed of live births, fetal deaths, and abortions, with rates and maternal demographic distributions.
variables.unit: pregnancies; pregnancies per 1,000 females in stated age group
variables.universe: report-defined pregnancies to Delaware residents
variables.suppression_rules: Report/table confidentiality and small-number footnotes apply.
variables.comparability_notes: Pregnancy is broader than live birth; verify fetal-death threshold and residence rules before comparing years or sources.

variables.label: Infant, neonatal, and postneonatal mortality rates
variables.definition: Deaths before age 1 per 1,000 live births, with neonatal and postneonatal components, causes, and demographic/risk-factor tables.
variables.universe: resident infant deaths and live births in the report's linked/period definition
variables.suppression_rules: Small counts/rates may be suppressed or aggregated; follow each table footnote.
variables.comparability_notes: Align period-linked versus cohort-linked method, pooled years, weighting, and race classification with HRSA/AHR/March of Dimes.

variables.label: Deaths, crude and age-adjusted mortality rates
variables.definition: Resident death counts and cause-specific crude or age-adjusted rates; age-adjusted rates use the 2000 U.S. standard population.
variables.universe: Delaware resident deaths in stated year/period
variables.suppression_rules: Report warns that rates based on fewer than 20 deaths are unreliable/not shown in affected charts/tables; exact rule follows table footnote.
variables.comparability_notes: Age-adjusted and crude rates are not interchangeable. Cause groups are ICD-10 based and differ from police complaint categories.

variables.label: Life expectancy at birth
variables.definition: Expected years of life at birth under mortality rates observed for the report period.
variables.universe: Delaware resident population/deaths in life-table period
variables.time_granularity: annual or pooled period specified by table
variables.comparability_notes: Not the same as mean age at death; compare only like-period life-table estimates.

crosswalk_hints.notes: Potential match to HRSA/AHR/March of Dimes; require same linkage method, years, residence, race categories, and weighting.

crosswalk_hints.notes: Strong conceptual match to CHR/HRSA/AHR; harmonize known-weight denominator and pooling.

source_variable_names: Birth outcome tables: birth weight and gestational age
crosswalk_hints.notes: Match March of Dimes only if obstetric gestational-age estimate and denominator treatment agree.

variables.source_variable_name: Average Monthly Employment / Average Annual Employment
variables.label: Covered employment by industry
variables.definition: Average number of workers covered by unemployment insurance who worked or received pay during the pay period including the 12th of the month; annual average is based on monthly levels.
variables.universe: QCEW-covered establishments and jobs; excludes self-employed, most unpaid family workers, armed forces, and other specified exclusions
missing_codes: blank or `*` in disclosure-protected report cells
variables.suppression_rules: QCEW disclosure rules protect identifiable employers; report uses `*` for suppressed/unavailable city detail.
variables.comparability_notes: Counts jobs by place of work; a person with multiple covered jobs is counted multiple times. Do not compare directly to LAUS/ACS employed persons.

variables.source_variable_name: Average Annual Wage; Total Quarterly Wages
variables.label: QCEW wages
variables.definition: Total covered-worker compensation paid during the period and annual average wage derived from total wages and employment; wages include bonuses, stock options, severance, tips, and other cash remuneration but exclude employer benefit contributions.
variables.unit: current dollars per worker; total dollars
variables.universe: QCEW-covered jobs/establishments
variables.comparability_notes: Average wage is not median worker earnings, household income, or average renter wage; industry composition affects comparisons.

variables.label: Industry classification
variables.definition: North American Industry Classification System code and corresponding industry title used to organize employment, wage, and GDP tables.
variables.universe: published establishments/industries
variables.suppression_rules: Detail can be suppressed where disclosure risk exists.
variables.comparability_notes: NAICS revisions and report aggregation can create series breaks; retain code and vintage, not label alone.

variables.source_variable_name: Civilian labor force; Employment; Unemployment; Unemployment rate
variables.label: LAUS labor-force measures
variables.definition: Resident civilian labor force equals employed plus unemployed persons; unemployed persons have no job, are available, and actively sought work under BLS definitions; rate is unemployed divided by civilian labor force.
variables.universe: civilian noninstitutional population age 16+ under CPS/LAUS concepts
variables.comparability_notes: Residence-based persons differ from QCEW payroll jobs. ACS unemployment is a survey-period estimate and may differ from monthly/annual LAUS.

variables.label: Labor-force participation
variables.definition: Civilian labor force as a percentage of the civilian noninstitutional population age 16 and over.
variables.universe: civilian noninstitutional population age 16+
variables.comparability_notes: Denominator includes people not in labor force; not the employment-population ratio or unemployment rate.

variables.label: Employment/wage change and rank
variables.definition: Arithmetic difference, percentage change between labeled periods, and ordering of industries/areas shown in report tables.
variables.universe: same as referenced parent measure
missing_codes: `*` or blank where unavailable/disclosure-protected or denominator unsuitable
variables.comparability_notes: A percentage change is not a percentage-point change; inspect exact start/end periods and revisions.

variables.source_variable_name: Gross Domestic Product; GDP by Industry
variables.label: Real/current-dollar state GDP
variables.definition: Value added from production in Delaware overall and by industry under BEA state GDP accounting; report distinguishes measure/price basis in table labels.
variables.unit: dollars (often millions), chained dollars, or percent change as labeled
variables.universe: economic production located in Delaware
variables.comparability_notes: Real and current-dollar GDP are not interchangeable; GDP is production, not wages or household income.

variables.label: Population and migration
variables.definition: Population estimate/change and domestic/international migration components from Census Population Estimates used in the report.
variables.universe: Delaware resident population
variables.comparability_notes: Population-estimate vintages revise prior years; distinguish net migration from gross in/out migration.

source_variable_names: Civilian labor force; Employment; Unemployment; Unemployment rate
crosswalk_hints.notes: Preferred official monthly/annual labor-market series; align residence, age 16+, period, seasonal adjustment, and revision with CHR/AHR/ACS.

Civilian labor force; Employment; Unemployment; Unemployment rate

source_variable_names: Average Annual Wage; Total Quarterly Wages

variables.source_variable_name: FAD observation fields: State; Year; Stratifier; Estimate; Standard Error; Lower/Upper CI; Numerator; Denominator; Notes
variables.label: Federally Available Data observation
variables.definition: Companion-file fields identify state, year, subgroup, estimate, uncertainty, numerator/denominator, and data notes for a named NOM/NPM/standardized measure.
variables.universe: one measure-state-year-stratifier observation
variables.suppression_rules: Subgroup estimates may be unavailable for insufficient sample; FAD cautions about wide CIs, including intervals >20 percentage points or >1.2 times the estimate in applicable displays.
variables.comparability_notes: Retain measure ID, source, year span, stratifier, numerator/denominator, and note fields together.

variables.label: Infant mortality
variables.definition: Infant deaths from birth to before age 1 divided by live births and multiplied by 1,000; linked birth/infant-death data and weights are used as specified.
variables.universe: live births and infant deaths under linked-file rules
variables.time_granularity: annual; commonly pooled three-year subgroup estimates
variables.suppression_rules: Small samples may be pooled or not shown; linked-death weights and notes apply.
variables.comparability_notes: Align linked/period method, pooled years, race categories, and weights with Delaware Vital/AHR/March of Dimes.

variables.label: Teen births
variables.definition: Live births to females age 15-19 divided by the female population age 15-19 and multiplied by 1,000.
variables.universe: females age 15-19 and births to that age group
variables.comparability_notes: Do not compare with pregnancy rate (includes other outcomes) or percentage of births to teens.

variables.source_variable_name: Breastfeeding initiation; exclusive breastfeeding through 6 months
variables.label: Breastfeeding
variables.definition: Initiation is ever breastfed by hospital discharge among live births in natality data; exclusive-through-six-months is an NSCH child measure among children old enough to observe the interval.
variables.universe: live births for initiation; children roughly 6 months through age 2 for duration measure under NSCH definition
variables.comparability_notes: Initiation and exclusive duration are distinct measures with different sources and universes; AHR 'Breastfed' label must be disambiguated.

variables.label: Children with a medical home
variables.definition: NSCH composite requiring a personal doctor/nurse, usual source of sick care, family-centered care, needed referrals, and effective care coordination; `MedicalHome_1` is the CSHCN subgroup form.
variables.universe: children age 0-17; CSHCN subgroup for MedicalHome_1
variables.comparability_notes: Referral wording changed in 2018 and the CSHCN definition expanded in 2025; preserve version when trending or matching AHR Medical Home.

variables.label: Maternal smoking during pregnancy
variables.definition: Live births for which the mother reported smoking during pregnancy divided by live births and multiplied by 100, under natality-file field definitions.
variables.universe: live births with maternal smoking information
missing_codes: unknown/not stated handled per natality source
variables.comparability_notes: Not the same as March of Dimes smoking in the 3 months before pregnancy, BRFSS adult current smoking, household smoke, or e-cigarette use.

variables.label: Birth outcomes
variables.definition: Percentage of live births below 2,500 grams and percentage before 37 completed weeks under national vital-statistics definitions.
variables.universe: live births with known birth weight or gestational age
variables.comparability_notes: Align gestational-age measure, known-value denominator, period, and race categories with Delaware Vital/CHR/AHR/March of Dimes.

variables.label: Title V program reach and finance
variables.definition: Application/reporting forms describe counts/percentages of mothers, infants, children, children with special health-care needs, and others served, plus funding/expenditure amounts by source/category.
variables.universe: people receiving report-defined Title V-supported services and fiscal-year program accounts
variables.comparability_notes: People served may overlap categories and are program reach, not population prevalence; fiscal figures differ from service counts and NOM/NPM outcomes.

crosswalk_hints.notes: Match linked-file method, weighting, pooled period, and strata to Delaware Vital/AHR/March of Dimes.
Match <37 completed weeks and obstetric-estimate/unknown handling.
Do not crosswalk to pre-pregnancy smoking without relabeling the exposure window.
Exact composite/version required; CSHCN subgroup is separate.

variables.source_variable_name: overall food insecurity rate; overall food insecure persons
variables.label: Overall local food insecurity
variables.definition: Modeled percentage and count of all people experiencing food insecurity in the year; local rates apply coefficients from state CPS relationships to ACS/BLS county or congressional-district predictors.
variables.data_type: numeric percent and integer modeled count
variables.universe: total resident population
variables.geography: county, congressional district, state, U.S.; food-bank service area aggregations
missing_codes: not available where required inputs absent
variables.suppression_rules: Model imputes some missing/negative ACS predictors; technical brief documents conditions. Estimates are approximations, not direct local survey prevalence.
variables.comparability_notes: Comparable mainly across similar geographies in one year. 2020-method estimates (2018 data) and later should not be compared with pre-2020 method estimates.

variables.source_variable_name: child food insecurity rate; child food insecure persons
variables.label: Child food insecurity
variables.definition: Modeled percentage/count for children, using household-with-children predictors except unemployment and disability, which use the full local population.
variables.data_type: numeric percent and integer modeled count
variables.universe: children/local child population under study definition
variables.suppression_rules: Model/imputation rules in technical brief apply.
variables.comparability_notes: Not interchangeable with household food insecurity or overall-person rate; predictor universes differ.

variables.label: Race/ethnicity food insecurity
variables.definition: Modeled subgroup-specific rate for Black (all ethnicities), Hispanic/Latino, and non-Hispanic white populations using subgroup-specific economic predictors.
variables.universe: specified race/ethnicity subgroup
missing_codes: not available for many geographies due to small state or county samples/populations
variables.suppression_rules: Not produced everywhere; technical brief reports 90% confidence intervals and warns that small samples increase uncertainty.
variables.comparability_notes: Race/ethnicity models differ from overall/child models and lack the non-undergraduate poverty adjustment; do not rank small differences without uncertainty.

variables.source_variable_name: senior food insecurity rate; older adult food insecurity rate
variables.label: Senior and older-adult food insecurity
variables.definition: Food insecurity estimates for seniors age 60+ and older adults age 50-59 produced directly from 2018-2023 CPS-FSS and geographic modeling/crosswalk methods described in the appendix.
variables.universe: seniors 60+ or older adults 50-59
variables.geography: national, state, and select metro areas/local outputs where supported
missing_codes: not available for unsupported local areas
variables.suppression_rules: Availability/precision rules differ from overall and child models.
variables.comparability_notes: Method differs from overall/child MMG estimates; do not assume county coverage or the same predictive model.

variables.label: Food-insecure people by likely nutrition-program income eligibility
variables.definition: Estimated share/count of food-insecure people below and above state-specific gross SNAP thresholds and other nutrition-program thresholds; Delaware's 2025 analysis uses a 200% of poverty SNAP gross-income threshold effective October 2024.
variables.universe: modeled food-insecure overall/child population
categories: between SNAP threshold and 185% poverty where relevant
variables.comparability_notes: Income eligibility is not actual program participation; applicants face additional net-income/asset/categorical rules. Thresholds vary by state and release.

variables.label: Additional dollars needed to be food secure
variables.definition: Localized annual need = per-person weekly CPS shortfall × 52 × 7/12 × modeled food-insecurity rate × population, adjusted by local food-cost index.
variables.unit: dollars per food-insecure person per week and total dollars per year
variables.universe: people in food-insecure households responding to CPS shortfall items; localized modeled population
missing_codes: missing CPS shortfall responses excluded under 2025 method
variables.suppression_rules: No public small-cell field rule found; model/missing rules documented in technical brief.
variables.comparability_notes: 2025 release changed from household weights/zero assignment to individual weights/exclusion of missing; 2023-or-later shortfall estimates are not comparable with estimates before 2022 as stated by publisher.

variables.label: Local relative food cost and meal cost
variables.definition: NielsenIQ county market-basket cost for 24 USDA Thrifty Food Plan categories plus applicable grocery taxes is converted to a relative index; national weekly food spending by food-secure people divided by 21 is adjusted by this index for local meal cost.
variables.universe: UPC-coded grocery sales/food-secure CPS spending under method
missing_codes: county food-cost input may be imputed
variables.suppression_rules: For counties below 20,000 population, market-basket price uses the county plus contiguous-county average; full imputation list is available only on request.
variables.comparability_notes: Meal cost is an modeled adequate-diet spending benchmark, not FMR/food benefit or actual spending of food-insecure households.

crosswalk_hints.notes: Keep person/child/subgroup modeled rates separate from AHR household survey prevalence and CHR composite Food Environment Index.
Not a general poverty rate or actual SNAP enrollment; denominator is food-insecure persons.
Can compare geography within an edition; do not treat as a household food budget or CPI.

sources.research_notes: Dataset-family scope includes requested tabular data, interactive-map outputs, report aggregates, and modeled estimates. The full dataset is request-mediated and no standalone public field-level dictionary was located, so status is partial published despite an unusually detailed public technical brief. 2025 means release year; estimates primarily describe 2023.

codebook_artifacts.notes: Use the edition-specific technical notes; current page updates yearly.

variables.label: Preterm birth
variables.definition: Live births before 37 completed weeks based on obstetric estimate of gestational age divided by live births with known gestational age, multiplied by 100.
variables.universe: live births with known obstetric gestational age
missing_codes: unknown gestational age excluded from denominator
variables.suppression_rules: Race/ethnicity and payer groups shown only with at least 10 observations under technical notes.
variables.comparability_notes: May differ from Delaware DPH due to submission timing/missing handling. Match obstetric estimate and known-age denominator with Vital/HRSA/AHR.

variables.source_variable_name: preterm birth grade; preterm birth rank
variables.label: Preterm birth grade and rank
variables.definition: Grade A through F with +/- based on deviation from the 8.1% goal using the standard deviation of 2014 state/DC rates; rank orders rounded rates from lowest to highest.
variables.universe: states, DC, Puerto Rico where comparable
variables.suppression_rules: Not ranked without available comparable data.
variables.comparability_notes: Grade is a transformation, not an outcome rate; ties share rank and the next rank is skipped.

variables.source_variable_name: preterm birth by maternal race/ethnicity; insurance payer
variables.label: Preterm birth disparities
variables.definition: Three-year 2022-2024 preterm rates by bridged maternal race/Hispanic ethnicity and payer at birth; payer is private, Medicaid, or other.
variables.universe: live births with known gestational age and subgroup/payer
variables.suppression_rules: Group shown only if it has at least 10 observations.
variables.comparability_notes: Pooled subgroup rate should not be compared as a single-year value; Hispanic and non-Hispanic race categories follow bridged natality conventions.

variables.source_variable_name: infant mortality rate; infant mortality rank; leading causes
variables.label: Infant mortality
variables.definition: Infant deaths divided by live births ×1,000 using 2023 NCHS period-linked birth/infant-death data; leading causes use 2021-2023 linked files and ICD-10 groupings.
variables.unit: deaths per 1,000 live births; rank; percent of infant deaths
variables.universe: live births/infant deaths in period-linked files
variables.suppression_rules: Race/ethnicity shown only with at least 10 infant deaths; weights account for unlinked deaths.
variables.comparability_notes: Align period-linked method, weights, years, and subgroup categories with Vital/HRSA/AHR.

variables.label: Maternal mortality
variables.definition: Deaths from pregnancy/childbirth complications during pregnancy or within 6 weeks, with underlying ICD-10 A34, O00-O95, or O98-O99, divided by births ×100,000.
variables.universe: qualifying maternal deaths and births
variables.suppression_rules: State/subgroup rates suppressed when deaths are insufficient for reliable estimates.
variables.comparability_notes: This is the NCHS maternal mortality definition, not pregnancy-related death within one year or all deaths of recently pregnant persons.

variables.label: Prenatal care
variables.definition: APNCU adequacy combines initiation, visits, and gestational age; inadequate is <50% expected visits or start in/after month 5; adequate is 80-109% and start before month 5, with adequate-plus >110%; initiation measures first-trimester start.
variables.universe: live births with complete initiation and visit data
variables.suppression_rules: Race groups shown with at least 10 observations.
variables.comparability_notes: Adequacy and initiation are distinct; do not crosswalk first trimester directly to APNCU adequate.

variables.source_variable_name: low-risk Cesarean birth rate; severe maternal morbidity
variables.label: Delivery outcomes
variables.definition: Low-risk Cesarean is Cesarean among nulliparous, term (≥37 weeks), singleton, vertex births; severe maternal morbidity is unexpected labor/delivery outcomes per 10,000 in-hospital deliveries excluding blood transfusions.
variables.unit: percent of NTSV births; events per 10,000 deliveries
variables.universe: NTSV live births; in-hospital deliveries for SMM
variables.time_granularity: 2024 natality for Cesarean; HCUP year shown for SMM
variables.comparability_notes: NTSV Cesarean is not overall Cesarean. SMM exclusion of transfusion and delivery-only denominator must be retained.

variables.source_variable_name: smoking before pregnancy; pre-pregnancy hypertension; pregnancy hypertension; unhealthy pre-pregnancy weight; pre-pregnancy diabetes
variables.label: Maternal chronic/risk conditions
variables.definition: Percent of live births exposed to each non-mutually-exclusive certificate condition; smoking means any cigarettes in 3 months before pregnancy, unhealthy weight means BMI <18.5 or ≥30, and diabetes excludes gestational diabetes.
variables.universe: live births with corresponding maternal certificate field
variables.comparability_notes: Smoking window is pre-pregnancy, unlike HRSA smoking during pregnancy; conditions overlap and must not be summed.

variables.source_variable_name: Medicaid postpartum extension; Medicaid expansion; paid leave; doula reimbursement; MMRC; postpartum mental-health screening
variables.label: Maternal health policy indicators
variables.definition: State policy statuses using specified external authoritative trackers and categories as assessed September 26, 2025.
variables.universe: states/DC/territories where applicable
variables.comparability_notes: Policy adoption does not measure implementation quality, utilization, or health outcome; each indicator has a different source/category set.

crosswalk_hints.notes: Match <37 weeks, obstetric estimate, known-GA denominator, data year, and pooled subgroup years.
Match period-linked file, weighting, and period to Delaware Vital/HRSA/AHR.
Exposure is 3 months before pregnancy; deliberately not equivalent to HRSA smoking during pregnancy.
Only crosswalk to NTSV Cesarean, not all Cesareans.

sources.research_notes: Dataset-family scope is the state report card plus its shared technical notes, national comparisons, and policy indicators. The report card mixes 2024 natality, 2023 infant mortality, 2019-2023 maternal mortality, and other source years; never label all values as 2025 data.

variables.label: Total population estimate and margin of error
variables.definition: ACS estimate of total population and its 90% margin of error from DP05 Sex and Age.
variables.universe: total population
variables.geography: state through tract and other ACS 5-year geographies
missing_codes: annotation/jam value when estimate unavailable; consult 2024 Jam Values
variables.suppression_rules: ACS data-release rules and annotation fields apply.
variables.comparability_notes: Five-year estimate is a period estimate, not a 2024 point count; do not compare overlapping five-year periods as independent observations.

variables.source_variable_name: DP05 sex, age, race, and Hispanic-origin profile fields
variables.label: Demographic composition
variables.definition: DP05 publishes count/percent estimates and margins of error for sex, age, race, Hispanic origin, and combined race/ethnicity categories.
variables.data_type: integer counts and numeric percents with MOEs
variables.universe: table-row-specific total population or sex/age/race universe
variables.time_granularity: one-year or five-year period depending endpoint
variables.comparability_notes: Race-alone, race-in-combination, and Hispanic-origin measures overlap differently; never crosswalk by a short label without the full API label/universe.

variables.label: Households and family composition
variables.definition: Total households and profile counts/percents for married/cohabiting, children, people 65+, living alone, household size, and related family characteristics.
variables.data_type: integer counts and numeric percents with MOEs
variables.universe: occupied housing units/households or families as full label states
variables.comparability_notes: Household, family, and person denominators differ; preserve full hierarchical label.

variables.label: Median household and per-capita income
variables.definition: Median household income and per-capita income in 2024 inflation-adjusted dollars, each with margin of error.
variables.universe: households for median household income; population for per-capita income
missing_codes: annotation/jam values including top/bottom/open interval flags where applicable
variables.comparability_notes: These two income measures have different units/denominators and neither equals QCEW wage or NLIHC renter wage; adjust dollar year across vintages.

variables.label: Population below poverty
variables.definition: Percent of all people whose income in the past 12 months is below the applicable poverty threshold, with percent margin of error.
variables.universe: population for whom poverty status is determined
variables.comparability_notes: Poverty threshold is not 30%/50% AMI, SNAP eligibility, or Feeding America food-insecure income band.

variables.label: Labor force, employed, unemployed, and unemployment rate
variables.definition: ACS profile estimates for population 16+ in labor force, civilian employed/unemployed persons, and unemployment rate among the civilian labor force.
variables.universe: population age 16+ or civilian labor force as full label states
variables.comparability_notes: ACS period estimate differs from official monthly/annual DOL LAUS; both count resident persons, unlike QCEW workplace jobs.

variables.label: Health-insurance coverage and no coverage
variables.definition: Counts/percents for the civilian noninstitutionalized population with/no coverage and separate under-19 universe/without-coverage fields.
variables.data_type: integer counts and numeric percents with MOEs
variables.universe: civilian noninstitutionalized population, or under age 19 for child fields
variables.comparability_notes: Universe differs from BRFSS 18-64 and CHR under-65 measures. People with multiple coverage types can appear in both private and public subcategories but only once in with-coverage total.

variables.source_variable_name: DP04_0001E; DP04_0002E/PE; DP04 tenure profile fields
variables.label: Housing units, occupancy, and homeownership
variables.definition: Total housing units, occupied/vacant status, and owner/renter-occupied tenure estimates with percents/MOEs.
variables.universe: housing units or occupied housing units as full label states
variables.comparability_notes: Homeownership is owner-occupied units divided by occupied units, not homeowners divided by persons.

variables.label: Gross rent as percent of household income
variables.definition: Renter-occupied units paying cash rent with computable GRAPI, including 30.0-34.9% and 35.0%+ bins.
variables.data_type: integer counts and numeric percents with MOEs
variables.universe: occupied units paying rent, excluding units where GRAPI cannot be computed
variables.comparability_notes: 30%+ burden requires combining DP04_0141 and DP04_0142 bins; severe 50%+ cannot be recovered from DP04's 35%+ top bin and needs a different table/microdata.

variables.label: Estimate, margin-of-error, percent, and annotation fields
variables.definition: API suffixes distinguish estimate, 90% MOE, percent estimate, percent MOE, and annotation companions.
variables.universe: all ACS table/profile variables
missing_codes: Jam Values workbook defines special numeric/character absence values
variables.suppression_rules: Data release rules and annotations explain unavailable estimates.
variables.comparability_notes: Never compare MOE as an estimate or treat API special numeric values as real data; preserve annotations.

crosswalk_hints.notes: Choose total civilian noninstitutionalized or under-19 universe explicitly before matching BRFSS/CHR/AHR.
ACS period estimate; compare to DOL LAUS only with clear methodological labeling.
ACS DP04 supports 30%+ renter burden but not 50%+ from profile bins; differs from CHR composite and NLIHC affordability benchmark.
Many other sources use ACS estimates as denominator/predictors; match vintage and geography.

sources.research_notes: Dataset-family scope is broad: the catalog profile is a UI over ACS profile/detailed/subject tables and possibly other Census products. This dictionary focuses on the ACS 2024 5-year profile fields corresponding to catalog measures and points to the complete API/PUMS dictionaries. Census profile variables are fully public; no inferred variable names are needed.

codebook_artifacts.applies_to: Delaware 2025 state facts and affordability measures
codebook_artifacts.notes: Two-page state factsheet with formulas/assumptions and Delaware values.

codebook_artifacts.applies_to: Delaware state, metro/HMFA, and county Out of Reach fields
codebook_artifacts.notes: Public machine-readable state workbook linked by the 2025 state page.

codebook_artifacts.title: Out of Reach 2025 Full Report
codebook_artifacts.applies_to: Definitions, sources, calculations, limitations, and all jurisdictions
codebook_artifacts.notes: Appendices explain FMR, AMI, wages, ACS renter counts, minimum wages, SSI, and cross-edition cautions.

codebook_artifacts.title: Out of Reach Delaware interactive page
codebook_artifacts.applies_to: Current Delaware state/area comparisons and downloads
codebook_artifacts.notes: Current page now displays 2026 data; use archived 2025 artifacts for the catalog's 2025 source.

variables.label: Fair Market Rent by bedroom size
variables.definition: HUD FY2025 estimate of gross rent (shelter plus tenant-paid utilities) for a modest unit, usually the 40th percentile for recent movers in an FMR area.
variables.universe: standard-quality recent-mover rental units under HUD FMR methodology
variables.geography: state weighted aggregate, metropolitan/HMFA, nonmetro county
missing_codes: †/footnote or not available as report states
variables.comparability_notes: FMR is not median rent paid by all renters and may be uniform within an FMR area. HUD methodology changes make cross-edition changes partly methodological.

variables.label: Housing Wage
variables.definition: Hourly wage a household must earn working 40 hours/week, 52 weeks/year so FMR plus utilities is no more than 30% of gross income; equivalently FMR ×12 /0.30 /2,080.
variables.universe: hypothetical full-time worker household
variables.comparability_notes: Normative affordability wage, not observed wage. Delaware two-bedroom value is $32.18 in 2025; distinguish from 2026 current page.

variables.source_variable_name: Annual income needed to afford FMR; rent affordable at income/wage
variables.label: Affordable-income and affordable-rent calculations
variables.definition: Annual income needed equals FMR ×12 /0.30; monthly affordable rent equals annual income ×0.30 /12 for AMI, 30%/50% AMI, minimum-wage, mean-renter-wage, or SSI scenarios.
variables.universe: hypothetical household at specified income
variables.comparability_notes: This is a calculated affordability ceiling, not observed rent burden or rent paid.

variables.label: Renter households
variables.definition: Number of renter-occupied households and share of total occupied households using 2019-2023 ACS estimates in 2025 tables.
variables.universe: occupied households
variables.comparability_notes: Households, not persons or rental units. Use same ACS vintage when comparing Census DP04.

variables.source_variable_name: Renter households below 30% AMI / below 50% AMI
variables.label: Extremely/very low-income renter households
variables.definition: Count and percent of renter households below 30% and 50% of area median income under HUD income-limit concepts.
variables.universe: renter households
variables.comparability_notes: 30% AMI is an area-relative income category, not federal poverty, 30% housing-cost burden, or Feeding America program threshold.

variables.source_variable_name: Minimum wage; work hours/week; full-time jobs needed
variables.label: Minimum-wage affordability gap
variables.definition: Higher of applicable federal/state/local minimum wage, plus hours per week or 2,080-hour-equivalent jobs required to afford bedroom-specific FMR at 30% of income.
variables.universe: hypothetical minimum-wage worker
variables.time_granularity: wage as of report cutoff/FY2025 FMR
variables.comparability_notes: Do not interpret jobs-needed ratio as actual household job count or labor-force statistic.

variables.label: Mean renter wage
variables.definition: Estimated hourly wage using BLS wage data adjusted by the ratio of renter-household income to overall household income from ACS and projected to 2025 as documented.
variables.universe: modeled wage of renters
variables.comparability_notes: Modeled mean is not BLS median occupational wage, QCEW average wage, or Census household income.

source_variable_names: Annual income needed to afford FMR
crosswalk_hints.notes: Normative FMR affordability calculations; not observed ACS/CHR/AHR burden prevalence.
Can align with ACS DP04 only using same ACS vintage and occupied-household denominator.

source_variable_names: Renter households below 30% AMI / below 50% AMI
crosswalk_hints.notes: AMI thresholds are area/family-size based and differ from poverty and food-program thresholds.

sources.research_notes: Dataset-family scope is the 2025 state workbook/factsheet plus full-report definitions. The live Delaware page has advanced to 2026, so archived URLs are required for reproducibility. The catalog mentions a shortage of affordable and available units, but that is primarily an NLIHC Gap measure; it was not identified as a standard 2025 Out of Reach Delaware workbook field and should not be inferred from renter counts.

codebook_artifacts.title: 2025 Calendar Year-End CompStat report
codebook_artifacts.applies_to: Citywide and district-level crime-complaint counts, shootings, periods, changes, and maps
codebook_artifacts.notes: Public table labels and caveats are available, but no offense-level dictionary, Delaware-code crosswalk, or machine-readable schema was found.

codebook_artifacts.title: WPD CompStat Reports and Crime Mapping
codebook_artifacts.applies_to: Current weekly and calendar-year-end CompStat reports and methodology overview
codebook_artifacts.notes: Explains near-real-time management purpose and links CrimeMapping.com search by neighborhood, address, offense, and date.

codebook_artifacts.title: WPD 2025 Year-End Report
codebook_artifacts.applies_to: 2025 preliminary reported offenses, shootings, victims, operations, and narrative definitions
codebook_artifacts.notes: Clarifies that CompStat captures preliminary reported offenses; final official jurisdiction statistics are later issued through FBI UCR.

variables.label: Violent crime complaints
variables.definition: Counts of WPD crime complaints classified under Delaware Criminal Codes into the named report rows; the report does not publish a statutory/offense inclusion crosswalk.
variables.universe: reported offenses recorded by WPD in Wilmington for the stated period
variables.time_granularity: last 7 days, last 28 days, year-to-date/calendar year
variables.suppression_rules: No count-suppression rule stated in the report.
variables.comparability_notes: Preliminary/revisable; Delaware-code categories explicitly differ from FBI UCR. Complaint count may differ from victims, incidents, arrests, charges, and death-certificate mortality.

variables.source_variable_name: Burglary; Felony Theft; Auto Theft; Theft (Misdemeanor)
variables.label: Property/theft crime complaints
variables.definition: Counts of WPD complaints in the named Delaware-code categories; felony and misdemeanor theft are separate rows.
variables.universe: reported offenses recorded by WPD in Wilmington
variables.comparability_notes: Do not combine felony/misdemeanor theft or treat WPD categories as FBI UCR without a published mapping.

variables.label: Total Part 1-style complaint rows
variables.definition: Sum displayed for murder, rape, robbery, aggravated assault, burglary, felony theft, and auto theft rows in the CompStat table.
variables.universe: the seven listed complaint categories, not all reported crime
variables.comparability_notes: Excludes misdemeanor theft and shooting rows; shootings can overlap offense categories. Never label as all crime.

variables.source_variable_name: Shooting Incidents; Shooting Victims; Juv Shooting Incidents; Juv Shooting Victims
variables.label: Shootings and victims
variables.definition: Counts of shooting incidents and people victimized; juvenile rows are subsets included in corresponding all-age totals.
variables.universe: WPD-recorded shootings/victims; juvenile subset under WPD operational definition
variables.comparability_notes: Victims can exceed incidents; juvenile counts must not be added to all-age totals. Shootings are not equivalent to firearm deaths or aggravated assaults.

variables.label: Comparison columns
variables.definition: Report columns compare current and prior counts for 7-day, 28-day, and YTD periods and show percentage changes versus prior years.
variables.universe: same category and comparable calendar window
missing_codes: *=percentage change unavailable/undefined in displayed table, commonly where a zero denominator prevents calculation
variables.suppression_rules: No suppression stated; asterisk semantics are not formally defined beyond table usage.
variables.comparability_notes: Use same closing date/window. Asterisk must not be parsed as zero percent.

variables.label: Normalized reporting window
variables.definition: Proposed comparison field mapping each repeated table block to `last_7_days`, `last_28_days`, or `year_to_date`.
variables.universe: each CompStat metric observation
variables.comparability_notes: Inferred normalization must retain report close date because YTD windows differ between weekly reports.
variables.inference_basis: The PDF repeats explicit `LAST 7 DAYS`, `LAST 28 DAYS`, and `YEAR TO DATE` headers but publishes no machine-readable field names; normalized codes are created for comparison.

variables.label: Complaint, incident, or victim denominator
variables.definition: Proposed semantic field distinguishing crime complaints, shooting incidents, and shooting victims.
variables.universe: each extracted report row
variables.comparability_notes: Required to prevent invalid sums/comparisons across superficially similar counts.
variables.inference_basis: The row labels and report narrative distinguish complaints, shooting incidents, and victims, but no formal schema field exists.

variables.label: Police district geography
variables.definition: Proposed district identifier extracted from the report header/map for district-specific pages.
variables.universe: WPD operational districts
missing_codes: citywide page may have no district
variables.comparability_notes: Police districts are operational geographies, not Census tracts/neighborhoods; boundaries may change and no GIS codebook was found.
variables.inference_basis: District labels and maps are printed in the PDF, but a public machine-readable geography schema/boundary crosswalk was not located.

crosswalk_hints.notes: WPD preliminary crime complaint/incident concept; do not equate to Vital Statistics homicide deaths or AHR/CHR mortality rates.
Keep incidents and victims separate; neither is firearm deaths.
Comparison to FBI UCR/NIBRS requires an explicit Delaware-code crosswalk not found publicly.

sources.research_notes: No public WPD data dictionary/codebook, statutory offense crosswalk, record layout, API schema, or GIS district boundary file was found. Public report row labels/caveats are marked published; only normalized comparison fields are marked inferred. Figures are posted about two weeks after the closing date, are preliminary and revisable, and explicitly differ from FBI UCR categories.
